title: Start a Web App
bottom_line: Run /plan-tools:create-webapp with a one-line idea, answer its questions up front, and Claude plans and builds a new FastAPI web app, committing as it goes.

sections.heading: Start in an empty folder with a one-line idea

blocks.code: /plan-tools:create-webapp [--host railway|generic] [--ai-model <openrouter model id>] [optional one-line app idea]
blocks.caption: Defaults: host railway, AI model openai/gpt-4o-mini.

blocks.title: Example
blocks.code: /plan-tools:create-webapp a recipe box where friends share weekly meal plans
blocks.caption: Starts a new web app, plans it, and implements it session by session.

blocks.title: The two optional flags
rows: With `generic`, every Railway setup and deploy step is skipped and you deploy to your own host. If you want mobile apps, Claude asks you for that host's public HTTPS address instead.
The OpenRouter model the app uses for its AI features.

blocks.text: Everything after the flags is your seed idea. Claude does not write app code itself. It gathers what its helpers need, removes everything that would stall them, then hands off planning and building.

blocks.title: When to use it
items: You want to start, bootstrap, kick off or build a new web app from scratch, planned and implemented end to end, not just scaffolded.
Even if you only say "new app", "build me an app that…" or "start a project for…".

terms.definition: The parts of the standard template your app actually needs, such as a database or AI.
A private file of settings and secret keys the app reads. It is never committed to git.
Something the unattended helpers cannot do themselves, such as an unreachable database or a missing key.
One chunk of the plan, sized to fit one Claude Code conversation.
A separate Claude helper started for one job, such as planning or building.

sections.heading: Check you have the tools and plugins it relies on

cards.title: fastapi-template and htmx-vs-alpine
cards.text: Required plugins from this marketplace. They install with plan-tools.

cards.title: railway plugin (optional)
cards.text: Its `use-railway` skill sets up the database and the deploy when the host is Railway. Without it, Claude skips that part and says so.

cards.title: capacitor plugins (optional)
cards.text: `capacitor-core` for building iOS/Android apps, and `capacitor-deployment` for store submission. Without them, Claude skips that part and says so.

cards.title: An empty project folder
cards.text: Claude confirms the current folder is the project root. If it is not empty, Claude stops and asks.

sections.heading: Claude asks everything up front, in as few rounds as it can

blocks.title: What Claude asks
rows: In kebab-case. Default: the current folder's name.

What the app must do, as concrete behaviour ("users log in with Google, create lists, share a list by link"), not categories ("auth", "CRUD"). Claude asks about anything unclear now, because the planner cannot ask you.
A link, a screenshot or image path, an app to imitate, or a few words ("minimal, dark, dense tables"). Without one, the planner picks a sensible default.
Should it also ship as iOS/Android apps? Yes or No, and which platforms.

Asked with the planning model: Everything (every open decision), Balanced (what you will see, or costly to undo) or Material only (choices that change direction or are hard to undo). The planner lists the rest as Assumed decisions.

blocks.text: Claude skips anything you already said.

sections.heading: Only the parts your features need are included

blocks.title: The parts Claude can include
rows: AI is included, or caching, rate limiting or background jobs are needed
Any feature generates, summarises, classifies or converses over text
The features need accounts or per-user data
Long-running or scheduled work; this implies Redis
blocks.caption: Claude decides each part from your features and confirms the table with you in one message.

blocks.text: Unused parts would add settings to fill in, services to run and dead code, so they are left out. Login state is kept in signed cookies.

cards.title: Server-rendered pages
cards.text: Jinja2 templates, HTMX for anything the server owns, Alpine.js for short-lived UI state. No single-page app and no JSON API for the browser.

cards.title: Visible errors
cards.text: Failed requests show visible feedback to the user across the whole app.

sections.heading: Say yes to mobile and iOS and Android apps are planned too

before.label: Mobile: No
before.text: None of the mobile steps on this page apply.

after.label: Mobile: Yes
after.text: A Capacitor shell whose WebView loads the deployed server is planned and built alongside the web app, so the FastAPI app stays the single source of the UI.

blocks.title: How the web app is made mobile-ready from session 1
items: A mobile-first responsive layout with safe-area spacing.
Every text input at 16px or larger, so iOS does not zoom in.
Boosted navigation on every page, so there is no white blink on each click.
Google login through a native sign-in step inside the app.
Native features such as camera, share, push and haptics through Capacitor plugins, with handling for denied permissions.

blocks.text: The mobile apps are part of the plan, not a later step.

sections.heading: You give the keys once; Claude writes and protects .env

blocks.title: The settings Claude collects
rows: you give it: `redis://localhost:6379` or a hosted address
you give them; they need an OAuth client in Google Cloud Console with `http://localhost:8000/auth/callback` as an authorised redirect URI
blocks.caption: Only the variables for the parts you included. Claude asks for them all in one message, each with a note on where it comes from.

steps.title: Starts git
steps.text: Runs `git init` if the folder is not already a repository.

steps.title: Writes .env
steps.text: With your values. From here on it never repeats a secret value back in the conversation.

steps.title: Hides .env from git
steps.text: Makes sure `.gitignore` lists `.env` (and `.prod.env`) and checks that `.env` is ignored. It is the one file that must never be committed.

steps.title: Writes .env.example
steps.text: The same keys with placeholder values.

sections.heading: Every outside service is tested before any building starts

blocks.text: The building helpers run unattended, so anything they cannot do themselves is done now.

blocks.title: What is checked

cards.title: Postgres reachable
cards.text: If the database does not exist yet, Claude creates it or has you set it up (on Railway with `use-railway`, if installed).

cards.title: Google OAuth client
cards.text: Redirect URI registered. You confirm this; it cannot be tested.

cards.title: Design reference readable
cards.text: The image path exists or the link opens.

cards.title: Mobile toolchain
cards.text: With mobile: Node and npm, Xcode and CocoaPods for iOS, Android Studio or the SDK for Android. Only your platforms.

cards.title: Deploy target
cards.text: With mobile: a public HTTPS address. A Railway project (with `use-railway`, if installed) or another host exists or can be created.

blocks.caption: Each one is actually tested and reported as pass or fail in a short checklist.

blocks.text: Claude also checks anything your features imply, such as third-party APIs, webhooks, domains or paid accounts. Without the `railway` plugin, the Railway parts are skipped and the report says so.

cards.title: A check fails
cards.text: Failures come as a numbered list, one line each.

points.text: Fix them and tell Claude you are done. It tests again.
It will not move on while a dependency is known to be broken.

sections.heading: A planner writes the plan and you approve it before splitting

nodes.label: Planner drafts plan
nodes.note: follows plan-helper at your question level, on your planning model

blocks.title: What the plan includes
items: A design brief, from your design reference or a restrained default.
For each interactive element, whether HTMX or Alpine.js handles it. Client-side choices follow the `htmx-vs-alpine` skill.
With mobile, a deploy step to Railway before the Capacitor work.

blocks.text: The plan is saved to `.planning/SPEC.md`. Claude asks the planner's questions in plain English and passes your answers back until the plan is finished. The planner asks only what your question level calls for and lists the rest in the plan under Assumed decisions.

after.label: Not split
after.text: The whole plan fits one session, and `.planning/SPEC.md` stays the single source.

blocks.caption: split-plan writes its files directly under `.planning/`.

sections.heading: Approve commits once, then helpers build the app

blocks.text: The one question: do you approve committing after every session (or at the end, if not split) without further confirmation? Nothing starts until you answer.

blocks.title: What each path does
items: Split: a helper on your implementing model runs /plan-tools:plan-split-implment, with a commit per session already approved, and reports the final progress and any session that stopped.

Not split: one helper on your implementing model builds the plan, checks it (`make dev` boots, migrations apply, each feature works), writes the project CLAUDE.md, commits and reports what was built and anything left undone. If it ends with a question, Claude asks you and passes the answer back.

sections.heading: You get the builder's report and any real next steps

cards.title: The builder's report
cards.text: Passed on to you as it is.

cards.title: Unresolved blockers
cards.text: Listed only if there are any.

cards.title: Deferred items
cards.text: Listed only if there are any.

cards.title: Store submission
cards.text: With mobile, submitting to the app stores is out of scope. Claude points to `capacitor-deployment:capacitor-app-store`, or says that plugin is not installed.

reference.title: About the plan-tools plugin
items: Plugin purpose: plan-driven workflow tools that bootstrap a new web or mobile app end to end, split implementation plans into context-sized resumable sessions, and drive them to PRs.
Installing plan-tools also installs the plugins it depends on: `ntfy`, `fastapi-template` and `htmx-vs-alpine`.

Default conventions: new web apps use FastAPI + Jinja2 + HTMX + Alpine.js, deployed to Railway, with OpenRouter `openai/gpt-4o-mini` (change with `--host generic` and `--ai-model <model id>`). Helpers run on `sonnet` unless you pick another model when asked.

No environment variables are needed for the plugin itself. The one setting, `designer_ui_review` (default `false`), is changed with `/plugin configure plan-tools@wovemind`. It runs the ui-change-guard designer review (/ui-change-guard:review-ui-change) before finalize-pr raises a PR.

next_action.text: In an empty folder, run /plan-tools:create-webapp followed by a one-line description of your app.
